places.name: Kopê House
places.signatureSubject: Short & Sweet (red bean–cherry espresso) / passion-fruit chocolate cappuccino
places.signatureRationale: Infatuation says offbeat signatures are the main draw (Short & Sweet; passion-fruit chocolate cappuccino); Eater highlights cocktail-style drinks from the founders’ pop-up era.

places.name: Hedge Coffee
places.signatureSubject: Redwood courtyard interior (tree Francesca through open roof)
places.signatureRationale: Eater, SF Standard, and Daily Coffee News all spotlight the Boor Projects woodsy interior and courtyard redwood as the permanent Mission café’s defining feature—matches Andy’s interior example.

places.name: The Coffee Movement
places.signatureRationale: Listed under Signature Drinks on the official menu as a dark-chocolate-dusted Australian-style cappuccino; dominates Yelp photo tags.

places.name: Bi-Rite Creamery
places.signatureRationale: Official Bi-Rite copy calls it “hands down our most popular”; Serious Eats and press treat it as the creamery’s calling card.

places.name: Jules
places.signatureSubject: Spicy Ronny (pepperoni + Calabrian heat / hot honey)
places.signatureRationale: Owner told Resy it’s the best seller; Infatuation and Bon Appétit On The Line highlight it as the house pepperoni pie.

places.name: Toronado
places.signatureSubject: Legendary draft-beer wall (~50 taps; Belgian + West Coast craft / Pliny culture)
places.signatureRationale: Craft Beer & Brewing and SFGATE frame Toronado as a monument to characterful draft beer; long associated with rare taps and Russian River/Pliny culture.

places.name: Flour + Water
places.signatureRationale: Eater’s Anatomy of a Dish and Chronicle pasta coverage treat tortellini en brodo as the year-round pasta centerpiece.

places.name: Original Joe's
places.signatureRationale: Wikipedia and house lore identify Joe’s Special as the namesake scramble; still a menu staple alongside Italian-American classics.

places.name: HK Lounge Bistro
places.signatureSubject: Baked BBQ pork buns (sugary crisp crust)
places.signatureRationale: Successor to Hong Kong Lounge; Infatuation and Michelin coverage spotlight the bakery-style char siu bao (XLB also excellent).

places.name: Taqueria El Farolito
places.signatureRationale: Infatuation and Mission consensus: charred-steak Mission burrito is the order; El Farolito’s own framing is Mission-style burrito identity.

places.name: San Tung
places.signatureRationale: Infatuation/Food GPS: SF’s most famous dry-fried wings; house Original Dry Fried Chicken.

places.name: Maison Nico
places.signatureRationale: Official shop and Chronicle/7x7 coverage: French pâté en croûte is the specialty (seasonal fillings).

places.name: Yank Sing
places.signatureSubject: Grandma Alice’s dumpling / cart dim sum ritual
places.signatureRationale: Official About and Time Out: multi-generation dim sum icon; Grandma Alice chicken-mushroom dumpling and Peking duck often cited as signatures.

places.name: Hook Fish Co.
places.signatureRationale: Infatuation: order a burrito stuffed with the daily catch; Eater/Thrillist frame the Outer Sunset sustainable seafood counter.

places.name: Cotogna
places.signatureSubject: Raviolo di ricotta (egg-yolk raviolo in brown butter)
places.signatureRationale: No SF “Catonia” found; Cotogna is the closest match. Chronicle calls Cotogna’s single giant ricotta–egg raviolo SF’s most famous pasta dish.

places.name: Tartine Bakery
places.signatureRationale: SFGATE/Goldbelly/Serious Eats: laminated cinnamon–orange morning bun is Tartine’s pastry signature (country loaf also iconic).

places.name: Mamahuhu
places.signatureRationale: Official Mamahuhu menu + Chronicle/Eater: Brandon Jew’s reinvented Chinese-American sweet-and-sour chicken is the headliner.

places.name: Nopalito
places.signatureRationale: Nopalito lore and PureWow recipe coverage: house chips tossed with chile de árbol, cotija, and crema—the shareable signature.

places.name: Nopa
places.signatureRationale: Eater’s iconic-meat map and long-running reviews: thick brined wood-oven pork chop is Nopa’s meat signature.

places.name: Saint Frank Coffee
places.signatureRationale: Condé Nast Traveler and Bon Appétit city guides call the espresso-over-tonic the house signature.

places.name: Molinari Delicatessen
places.signatureRationale: SFGATE “only one way to order” piece and SF guides: classic Italian cold-cut sandwich, often on Dutch crunch.

places.name: Ernest
places.signatureRationale: Resy, Infatuation, and Chronicle cite DIY tartare–ikura–nori handrolls as Ernest’s most-referenced signature.

places.name: Verjus
places.signatureRationale: Eater dining report and Infatuation: glossy garlic-herb Boursin omelet is the wine bar’s food signature.

places.name: Nopa Fish Market
places.signatureRationale: Chronicle and 7x7 on the Ferry Building opening: rockfish in Moroccan spice batter with harissa aioli is the headliner.

places.name: The Laundromat SF
places.signatureSubject: Detroit-style pizza (Holey Roller bagels by day)
places.signatureRationale: Eater and Bold Italic: former Outer Richmond laundromat known for Detroit pies and Holey Roller bagels.

places.name: Pearl 6101
places.signatureRationale: Infatuation and Eater: silky fazzoletti with white Bolognese is the recurring must-order.

places.name: Arsicault Bakery
places.signatureRationale: Infatuation, Bon Appétit, and Yelp-top-croissant press: almond croissant (and plain croissant) define Arsicault.

places.name: Flour + Water Pizzeria
places.signatureSubject: OG Osso (bone-marrow white pie) / cacio e pepe pizza
places.signatureRationale: Bold Italic/7x7/Chronicle: bone-marrow OG Osso is the dramatic dine-in signature; cacio e pepe often cited as bestseller.

places.name: Pabu Izakaya
places.signatureRationale: Forbes and Bold Italic: oyster topped with uni, ikura, tobiko, and ponzu crème fraîche is the signature bite.

places.name: Capo's
places.signatureRationale: Capo’s/Tony Gemignani site and USA Today: Chicago deep-dish is the raison d’être; Old Chicago is the flagship build.

places.name: Tartine Manufactory
places.signatureRationale: Same Tartine morning-bun signature, famously baked at the Manufactory; SFGATE covered the Mission production of the city’s morning buns.

places.name: Garden Creamery
places.signatureRationale: Timeout and shop reviews: Mission dairy-free creamery known for Asian-inspired flavors; salty kaya repeatedly called signature.

places.name: Liholiho Yacht Club
places.signatureRationale: Chronicle/SFist classic signature (misoyaki tongue in poppyseed bun); menu rotates—confirm current availability.

places.name: Tony's Pizza Napoletana
places.signatureRationale: Official Tony’s: limited Neapolitan Margherita that won in Naples; only ~73 made per day.

places.name: Loló
places.signatureRationale: Perfect Spot / early press: panko shrimp in thin jicama “tortillas” with tropical relish is Loló’s signature.

places.name: Deli Board
places.signatureRationale: Official menu and sandwich lore: the 49er is the stacked house monster; Allison also a top seller.

places.name: Delfina
places.signatureRationale: Chronicle recipe features and Eater reopen coverage: Mission spaghetti finished in reduced tomato sauce is Delfina’s iconic dish.

places.name: Tacolicious
places.signatureRationale: Tacolicious menu and reviews: traditional Coca-Cola-braised carnitas is the house classic taco.

places.name: Andytown Coffee Roasters
places.signatureRationale: Official Andytown identity and Yelp: espresso, sparkling water, brown sugar, whipped cream—the Outer Sunset signature bird drink.

places.name: RT Rotisserie
places.signatureRationale: 7x7 and Eater: buttermilk–porcini–Douglas-fir rotisserie bird is the whole concept.

places.name: House of Prime Rib
places.signatureRationale: Official HOPR and Infatuation: aged prime rib carved tableside with spinning salad, Yorkshire pudding, creamed spinach.

places.name: Foreign Cinema
places.signatureRationale: Official site and OpenTable/press: Mission courtyard with films on the back wall is the defining experience (sesame fried chicken also iconic).

places.name: Limón Rotisserie
places.signatureSubject: Pollo a la brasa / Ceviche Limón
places.signatureRationale: Official Limón menus: open-flame rotisserie chicken and house ceviche are the Peruvian signatures.

places.name: Kin Khao
places.signatureRationale: Michelin, Eater, and Condé Nast Traveler: spicy mushroom curry mousse with rice cakes is Kin Khao’s signature.

places.name: China Live
places.signatureRationale: OpenTable/Eater: SJB called the #1 seller / headliner of the Chinatown food hall.

places.name: R&G Lounge
places.signatureRationale: AP News, Condé Nast Traveler, and house menus: live crab with salt and pepper is the Chinatown signature plate.

places.name: Han Il Kwan
places.signatureRationale: Infatuation: classic Richmond Korean BBQ known for generous banchan and spicy pork/galbi.

places.name: Lovely's
places.signatureRationale: Infatuation: schmaltz-onion Drive-Thru smash is the Cole Valley order.

places.name: Two Pitchers Brewing Co.
places.signatureRationale: SFGATE, Infatuation, and official site: Outer Sunset taproom known for cheap Baseline Lager; food from Maillards on-site.

places.name: Maillards
places.signatureRationale: Chronicle, Infatuation, and Eater: caramelized-shallot double with Maillards sauce is the signature smash.

places.name: Day Moon
places.signatureRationale: Infatuation: a trip “isn’t complete” without the tangy sourdough baguettes at this Outer Sunset bakery.

places.name: Outerlands
places.signatureSubject: Levain toast with cultured butter & jam
places.signatureRationale: Michelin, Thrillist, and Infatuation: thick house levain toast is the Outer Sunset brunch signature.

places.name: Tony Nik's
places.signatureSubject: Classic martini in historic North Beach bar
places.signatureRationale: Tony Nik’s cafe history and SF Examiner: 1930s North Beach bar known for expert martinis and old-school vibe.

places.name: Trick Dog
places.signatureRationale: Imbibe and official site: twice-yearly conceptual menus are the bar’s signature—not one permanent drink.

places.name: True Laurel
places.signatureRationale: Imbibe recipe and Mission Local: gin/vermouth with house bay-laurel tincture is the namesake signature.

places.name: Penny Roma
places.signatureSubject: Agnolotti dal plin / rustic pasta program
places.signatureRationale: Chronicle opening coverage and Infatuation: Flour + Water sister’s rustic stuffed pastas; agnolotti often highlighted.

places.name: Bodega SF
places.signatureRationale: Infatuation: North Beach wine bar known for wild BTG pours and housemade Bodega Dawg; treat as Bodega Wine (not a separate restaurant).

places.name: Little Original Joe's
places.signatureRationale: House dinner menu and Forbes: Joe’s Classic Chicken Parm is the West Portal Italian-American signature.

places.name: Beit Rima
places.signatureRationale: Infatuation: mezze platter is “practically synonymous” with Beit Rima.

places.name: Farmhouse Kitchen Thai
places.signatureRationale: Timeout and Chronicle: Hat Yai fried chicken with blue rice and curry is Farmhouse Kitchen’s signature.

places.name: Daeho
places.signatureRationale: Infatuation, Goldbelly, and viral press: braised short-rib stew capped with torched cheese.

places.name: Burma Superstar
places.signatureRationale: Official menu and SFGATE: fermented tea-leaf salad mixed tableside made the Clement St. icon.

places.name: Burma Love
places.signatureRationale: Taste Edit / OpenTable: same family signature laphet thoke; garlic noodles also house-noted.

places.name: Taqueria El Buen Sabor
places.signatureRationale: Official El Buen Sabor site and local writeups highlight the al pastor burrito; Infatuation covers the Mission taqueria.

places.name: La Taqueria
places.signatureSubject: Carne asada burrito, no rice (El Dorado crisp optional)
places.signatureRationale: Infatuation, Bon Appétit, and Eater: riceless Mission burrito—often carne asada, optionally grill-crisped El Dorado-style.

places.name: Bottega
places.signatureRationale: Bottega Valencia: Roman-style pinsa is the concept; 48 Hills Best of Bay highlights pear–taleggio sachetti pasta.

places.name: Good Good Culture Club
places.signatureRationale: Resy, Eater, and Infatuation: deboned wing stuffed with sticky rice, double-fried, mango-adobo glaze—the bestseller.

places.name: Golden Boy Pizza
places.signatureRationale: Infatuation and KQED: fluffy square Sicilian-style slices (esp. pepperoni) are the North Beach late-night signature.

places.name: Comstock Saloon
places.signatureRationale: Punch: house bourbon–cherry sour topped with sparkling wine has been a top seller for a decade+.

places.name: Rampant Bottle & Bar
places.signatureRationale: Official About and Chronicle: Outer Richmond natural-wine bottle shop/bar; rotating small-production pours are the draw.

places.name: Ordinaire
places.signatureRationale: SFGATE “shrine to natural wine” plus Infatuation/Wikipedia: Grand Ave. Oakland natural-wine bar/shop (Bay Area list fixture).

places.name: Waystone
places.signatureSubject: Curated wine list + live jazz nights
places.signatureRationale: Official About/calendar: Causwells wine director’s list plus live jazz in North Beach.

places.name: Golden Sardine
places.signatureSubject: Riesling and tinned fish among poetry shelves
places.signatureRationale: Eater SF reported the owner's plan for 'an unreasonable amount of riesling' plus a tinned-fish shop, the Chronicle noted 10 Rieslings by the glass at opening, and The Infatuation describes drinking Riesling surrounded by poetry books.

places.name: Radhaus
places.signatureSubject: Bay-view hall with a Ponderosa pine bar
places.signatureRationale: Eater SF's review headline says the big, beautiful space is the draw, and Architectural Record calls the Ponderosa pine bar and communal bench the restaurant's signature elements.

places.name: The Interval
places.signatureSubject: Floor-to-ceiling library and 10,000 Year Clock prototypes
places.signatureRationale: Long Now's own page and Fast Company single out the floor-to-ceiling Manual for Civilization library, the Orrery, and the Chime Generator table as the room's defining features.

places.name: The Page
places.signatureSubject: Parklet built as a replica of the bar inside
places.signatureRationale: SFGATE calls it probably the coolest parklet in San Francisco, a reconstruction of the interior with a faux-brick wall and fireplace, and SFist calls it the most charming and clever pandemic-era parklet in the city.

places.name: Zam Zam
places.signatureRationale: The city's Legacy Business Registry report, Time Out, and the SF Examiner all name the gin martini as the house signature, and the Examiner explains the smaller 'Bruno' pour named for the late owner.

places.name: Mosto
places.signatureRationale: Mosto's own site calls its agave-spirits selection one of SF's best, and 2011 opening coverage (tablehopper, Thrillist) counted more than 300 tequilas and mezcals.

places.name: Self Edge
places.signatureRationale: Self Edge's own listing says it specializes in Japanese selvedge denim, most of it exclusive to the store in North America, and the SF Chronicle calls it San Francisco's Japanese denim mecca.

places.name: Ministry of Scent
places.signatureRationale: The shop's About page says it presents artistic scents from independent perfumers and niche houses, and The New Fillmore calls it an S.F. original known for its wide selection of niche and indie scent houses.

places.name: Stonemill Matcha
places.signatureRationale: Eater SF's opening coverage and the cafe's own site center it on stone-ground matcha from shade-grown Kyoto farms, served hand-whisked at a ceremonial counter or as lattes.

places.name: Evan Kinori
places.signatureRationale: The FT and SF Standard describe the store as the flagship for Kinori's soft, wide-cut, earth-toned clothing made from carefully sourced natural fabrics, shown alongside ceramics and furniture.

places.name: Rachel Comey
places.signatureRationale: The brand's own bio credits it with pioneering stacked-heel clogs and booties and cropped high-waist denim, and GQ and Vogue single out the wide-leg cropped Legion jean as its signature.

places.name: SF76
places.signatureRationale: The shop's own site names Hasami Porcelain, ARAS tableware, donabe, kitchen tools and incense as its core lines, and its FAQ steers visitors to compare Hasami Porcelain in store.

places.name: Song Tea & Ceramics
places.signatureSubject: Rare Chinese and Taiwanese teas and artist-made ceramics
places.signatureRationale: The shop's site, Fresh Cup and Time Out all describe small-batch teas sourced directly from producers in China and Taiwan, led by its flagship oolongs, sold alongside handmade ceramics from Taiwan, China and the US.

places.name: ReLove
places.signatureSubject: Curated designer, vintage and contemporary resale
places.signatureRationale: Time Out, InsideHook and the shop's own site describe a hand-picked mix of true vintage, designer and contemporary pieces for women and men.

places.name: Reliquary
places.signatureSubject: Antique jewelry and a 22K gold house line
places.signatureRationale: Time Out highlights the owner's trove of antique and vintage jewelry, and the shop's site leads with its 22K gold house-line strands and rings.

places.name: Heath Ceramics
places.signatureSubject: Heath tile and tableware (tile made on site)
places.signatureRationale: Heath's own San Francisco and factory-tour pages present the building as its tile factory and showroom, and 7x7 and The Bold Italic highlight watching tile production through glass from the showroom.

places.name: Dandelion Chocolate
places.signatureSubject: Single-origin chocolate bars and toasted-to-order s'mores
places.signatureRationale: Dandelion's Ferry Building page and its 2026 post single out its bean-to-bar chocolate bars, hot chocolate, and freshly toasted s'mores as the draws at this shop.

places.name: William Stout Architectural Books
places.signatureRationale: The shop's About page and SF Heritage describe it as one of only three US bookstores dedicated to architecture and design, stocking everything from rare books to contemporary monographs.

places.name: Shoji
places.signatureRationale: The SF Chronicle and Hoodline call the whipped-cream-topped matcha einspänner Shoji's viral signature; the Chronicle reports it sells more than 200 a day.

places.name: Alchemy Springs
places.signatureRationale: SFGATE, the SF Standard and Dwell all single out the circular, tiered sauna by architect Olle Lundberg, billed as the largest freestanding sauna in the country.

places.name: Golden Gate Park
places.signatureRationale: Gardens of Golden Gate Park calls it the oldest public wood-and-glass conservatory in North America and one of San Francisco's most photographed attractions; Wikipedia names it the park's oldest building.

places.name: Ocean Beach
places.signatureRationale: Wikipedia says Ocean Beach is known for its strong currents, surf culture, and foggy late-spring and summer weather; the NPS describes a 3.5-mile beach whose currents suit only experienced surfers.
